note: Folklore and legends, written as short original summaries. Not factual claims.

legends.name: Jersey Devil
legends.blurb: A winged, hoofed creature said to have been born in the Pine Barrens in the 1700s and to still roam the pines.

legends.name: Champ
legends.blurb: A long-necked lake monster people claim to have spotted in Lake Champlain for well over a century.

legends.name: Bennington Triangle
legends.blurb: An area around Glastenbury Mountain where several people vanished in the 1940s, fueling talk of a curse.

legends.name: Dover Demon
legends.blurb: A pale, big-headed figure with glowing eyes that teenagers reported seeing over two nights in 1977.

legends.name: Bridgewater Triangle
legends.blurb: A swampy stretch of Massachusetts with a long list of odd reports: lights, creatures and strange happenings.

legends.name: Lizzie Borden House
legends.blurb: The house where the Borden murders happened in 1892, now a bed and breakfast with plenty of ghost stories.

legends.name: Headless Horseman
legends.blurb: The village tied to the tale of a headless Hessian soldier riding through the night looking for his head.

legends.name: Amityville House
legends.blurb: A Long Island home whose 1970s haunting claims became one of the most famous ghost stories in the country.

legends.name: Melon Heads
legends.blurb: Local tales of small, large-headed figures said to lurk on back roads in the Connecticut woods.

legends.name: Snallygaster
legends.blurb: A dragon-like beast from German settlers' folklore said to swoop down from the skies over western Maryland.

legends.name: Maryland Goatman
legends.blurb: A half-man, half-goat figure said to haunt Fletchertown Road near Bowie.

legends.name: Eastern State Penitentiary
legends.blurb: A crumbling 1800s prison where visitors and staff describe footsteps, voices and shadowy figures.

legends.name: Gettysburg ghosts
legends.blurb: The Civil War battlefield is among the most ghost-storied places in America, from Devil's Den to old town houses.

legends.name: Squonk
legends.blurb: A sad, warty forest creature from lumberjack lore that supposedly dissolves into tears when cornered.

legends.name: Mothman
legends.blurb: A tall winged figure with red eyes reported in 1966-67, later tied to the Silver Bridge collapse.

legends.name: Flatwoods Monster
legends.blurb: A towering, glowing-eyed being that locals reported after seeing a light fall from the sky in 1952.

legends.name: Greenbrier Ghost
legends.blurb: A murdered woman whose ghost, as the story goes, helped convict her husband in an 1897 trial.

legends.name: Grafton Monster
legends.blurb: A pale, headless, seal-like figure a reporter said he saw by a riverside road in 1964.

legends.name: Brown Mountain Lights
legends.blurb: Mysterious glowing orbs reported for generations above Brown Mountain in the Blue Ridge.

legends.name: Lost Colony of Roanoke
legends.blurb: The English settlers who vanished in the 1580s, leaving only the word CROATOAN carved behind.

legends.name: Lizard Man of Scape Ore Swamp
legends.blurb: A green, scaly, seven-foot creature people said they saw around a South Carolina swamp in 1988.

legends.name: Bell Witch
legends.blurb: A spirit said to have tormented the Bell family in the early 1800s; a nearby cave keeps the legend going.

legends.name: Wampus Cat
legends.blurb: A shape-shifting cat-woman from Appalachian folklore said to prowl the hills at night.

legends.name: Pope Lick Monster
legends.blurb: A goat-man said to live under a railroad trestle; the legend has drawn people onto the dangerous bridge.

legends.name: Kelly-Hopkinsville encounter
legends.blurb: In 1955 a family said small goblin-like beings besieged their farmhouse all night.

legends.name: Skunk Ape
legends.blurb: Florida's swamp version of Bigfoot, known for a rotten smell and sightings around Ochopee.

legends.name: Coral Castle
legends.blurb: Tons of coral carved by one man working alone at night, which spawned claims of secret forces.

legends.name: Robert the Doll
legends.blurb: A straw-filled doll said to be cursed; visitors still write it letters asking for forgiveness.

legends.name: St. Augustine Lighthouse
legends.blurb: A lighthouse with stories of children's laughter and a keeper's ghost on the tower stairs.

legends.name: Cassadaga Spiritualist Camp
legends.blurb: A small town of mediums and psychics founded in the 1890s, with plenty of local ghost tales.

legends.name: Altamaha-ha
legends.blurb: A river monster said to swim the backwaters of coastal Georgia's Altamaha River.

legends.name: Sorrel-Weed House
legends.blurb: One of Savannah's best-known haunted homes, linked to a tragic 1800s family story.

legends.name: Rougarou
legends.blurb: A Cajun werewolf said to hunt the bayous, especially for anyone who skips Lent.

legends.name: Myrtles Plantation
legends.blurb: A plantation house famous for ghost stories, including a mirror said to hold spirits.

legends.name: LaLaurie Mansion
legends.blurb: A French Quarter mansion with a grim 1834 history and a long reputation for hauntings.

legends.name: Honey Island Swamp Monster
legends.blurb: A tall, gray-haired creature with webbed tracks reported in a Louisiana swamp since the 1960s.

legends.name: Fouke Monster
legends.blurb: A hairy swamp creature known locally as the Boggy Creek Monster; it inspired a 1972 film.

legends.name: Beast of Bray Road
legends.blurb: A wolf-like creature that walks upright, reported along a rural Wisconsin road since the 1980s.

legends.name: Hodag
legends.blurb: A horned, toothy beast 'discovered' in an 1890s hoax that the town adopted as its mascot.

legends.name: Michigan Dogman
legends.blurb: A dog-headed creature that stands on two legs, made famous by a 1987 radio song and later sightings.

legends.name: Piasa Bird
legends.blurb: A winged monster painted on the river bluffs, drawn from Native American imagery and local legend.

legends.name: Resurrection Mary
legends.blurb: A young woman in a white dress said to hitch rides near Resurrection Cemetery and then vanish.

legends.name: Enfield Horror
legends.blurb: A three-legged, gray creature a resident said attacked his house in 1973.

legends.name: Van Meter Visitor
legends.blurb: A winged creature with a glowing horn reported over several nights in 1903.

legends.name: Villisca Axe Murder House
legends.blurb: The home where eight people were killed in 1912, a crime never solved; overnight visitors report activity.

legends.name: Momo the Monster
legends.blurb: A hairy, foul-smelling creature reported around this river town in 1971.

legends.name: Loveland Frogman
legends.blurb: A frog-like humanoid that two police officers said they saw by a road in 1972.

legends.name: Ohio State Reformatory
legends.blurb: A castle-like former prison known for its ghost tours and its role in famous films.

legends.name: Bessie
legends.blurb: A big serpent-like creature people have reported in the waters of Lake Erie.

legends.name: Pukwudgie
legends.blurb: Small troublemaking beings from Wampanoag folklore, with reported sightings at Indiana's earthworks.

legends.name: Wendigo
legends.blurb: A cannibal spirit of winter from Algonquian tradition, linked to the northern woods and hunger.

legends.name: Marfa Lights
legends.blurb: Glowing orbs seen on the horizon east of Marfa, with a roadside viewing area for watchers.

legends.name: Chupacabra
legends.blurb: A blood-drinking creature from Latin American lore, with many Texas reports of mangy, hairless animals.

legends.name: Lake Worth Monster
legends.blurb: A goat-like creature reported around Greer Island in 1969.

legends.name: Aurora UFO incident
legends.blurb: An 1897 newspaper story of an airship crash whose 'pilot' was said to be buried in the town cemetery.

legends.name: La Llorona
legends.blurb: The weeping woman who searches rivers for her lost children; the story is told across the Southwest.

legends.name: Deer Woman
legends.blurb: A shape-shifting woman with deer hooves from many Native American traditions.

legends.name: Stull Cemetery
legends.blurb: A tiny cemetery that rumor calls one of the 'gates to hell'; the old church ruin is now gone.

legends.name: Thunderbird
legends.blurb: A powerful bird spirit from many Plains peoples' traditions, linked to storms and thunder.

legends.name: Skinwalker
legends.blurb: In Navajo tradition, a witch able to take animal form; a serious belief many prefer not to discuss.

legends.name: Phoenix Lights
legends.blurb: Thousands of people reported a huge V-shaped formation of lights over Phoenix in March 1997.

legends.name: Roswell incident
legends.blurb: The 1947 crash of what the military later called a balloon; it became the most famous UFO story ever.

legends.name: Dulce Base
legends.blurb: A conspiracy story about a secret underground facility beneath a mesa near Dulce.

legends.name: Stanley Hotel
legends.blurb: The hotel that inspired The Shining, known for nightly ghost tours.

legends.name: Bear Lake Monster
legends.blurb: A serpent-like creature first described in 1860s newspaper stories about the lake.

legends.name: Skinwalker Ranch
legends.blurb: A ranch whose owners and researchers describe lights, odd animals and unexplained events.

legends.name: Flathead Lake Monster
legends.blurb: A large creature reported in Montana's biggest natural lake since the late 1800s.

legends.name: Pedro Mountain mummy
legends.blurb: A tiny mummified figure found in a 1930s mining blast, fueling stories of little people.

legends.name: Tahoe Tessie
legends.blurb: A creature said to live in Lake Tahoe's deep, cold water.

legends.name: Area 51
legends.blurb: A secret Air Force testing site that became the center of alien-crash and cover-up stories.

legends.name: Mizpah Hotel Lady in Red
legends.blurb: A 1907 hotel said to be haunted by a woman killed there long ago.

legends.name: Si-Te-Cah giants
legends.blurb: Paiute stories of red-haired giants, tied to finds in a Nevada cave.

legends.name: Bigfoot (Patterson-Gimlin film)
legends.blurb: The spot where the famous 1967 footage of a walking Bigfoot was filmed.

legends.name: Winchester Mystery House
legends.blurb: A rambling mansion with stairs to nowhere, built nonstop for decades by Sarah Winchester.

legends.name: RMS Queen Mary
legends.blurb: A retired ocean liner turned hotel with many reports of ghosts in its pools and cabins.

legends.name: Alcatraz
legends.blurb: The former island prison where guards and visitors describe clanging doors and voices.

legends.name: Lemurians of Mount Shasta
legends.blurb: A legend of an ancient people said to live in tunnels beneath the volcano.

legends.name: Hotel del Coronado
legends.blurb: A grand 1888 hotel said to be haunted by a guest who died there in 1892.

legends.name: Cadborosaurus
legends.blurb: A sea serpent people have reported off the coasts of British Columbia and Washington.

legends.name: Kenneth Arnold sighting
legends.blurb: In 1947 a pilot said he saw nine fast objects near Mount Rainier; the press coined 'flying saucer'.

legends.name: Bigfoot in Skamania County
legends.blurb: A county that once passed an ordinance protecting Bigfoot from being killed.

legends.name: Crater Lake legends
legends.blurb: Klamath stories describe a battle between spirits that created the lake.

legends.name: Oregon Vortex
legends.blurb: A roadside attraction where people seem to change height, an optical illusion with a spooky reputation.

legends.name: Shanghai Tunnels
legends.blurb: Underground passages tied to stories of men kidnapped onto ships, now a ghost tour stop.

legends.name: Kushtaka
legends.blurb: A shape-shifting otter-man from Tlingit tradition said to lure people near the water.

legends.name: Night Marchers
legends.blurb: Spirits of ancient warriors said to march at night; tradition says not to look at them.

legends.name: Pele's curse
legends.blurb: The Hawaiian goddess of volcanoes; taking lava rocks home is said to bring her bad luck.

legends.name: Menehune
legends.blurb: A legendary people of small builders said to work only at night.
